published_odgi_arm_axis.quantity: odgi pangenome-graph node Jaccard DISTANCE between arm-level PHR sequence sets; similarity = 1 - d

diagonal_not_zero.note: the published matrix is not a proper metric: some arms have a non-zero self-distance (Jaccard of an arm's PHR set with itself < 1). Only off-diagonal cells are used by any statistic here.

pair_level_jaccard_axis.quantity: Jaccard SIMILARITY of the two PHR sequences of the pair

rederived_paf_jaccard_axis.claimed_by: M6 lane, as the 'maskable' substitute for the published axis

stored_validation.description: arm-level sequence-sharing Jaccard re-derived from the wfmash all-vs-all PAFs (>=95% identity blocks intersected with the called PHR regions), unmasked and with >=50%-satellite 5 kb bins removed

rederived_paf_jaccard_axis.cause: mouse_satellite_sensitivity.py:706 stores the PAF record as (qs, qe) = (int(c[1]), int(c[2])), but PAF column 2 (0-based index 1) is QLEN and index 2 is QSTART, so every interval is (qlen, qstart) with qlen > qstart; intersect_intervals() then finds no overlap and every derived Jaccard is 0.0

axis_identity_test.conclusion: the published arm-level odgi axis IS the arm-pair mean of the pair-level Jaccard column, so analyses (1) and (2) use the same underlying similarity axis; they differ in resolution (pair vs arm mean), not in axis
axis_identity_test.per_window_note: the published matrix is built from the 1 Mb flanks only, so at 2 Mb / 4 Mb the arm-mean pair Jaccard and the published axis are two genuinely different axes (they are still rank-equivalent at 4 significant digits or better, but not identical) -- that is the only place in the project where an axis change is even representable

distance_to_telomere.definition: min(phr_start, flank_len - phr_end) per PHR sequence, then the max over the two sequences of the pair -- i.e. how far the pair's PHRs reach inward from their telomeres
distance_to_telomere.conclusion: every PHR in these tables is telomere-anchored: 100.0% of pairs are within 10 kb and 70.3% within 1 kb of the telomere (max 4532 bp), so the referee's 'holding distance-to-telomere fixed' is satisfied by construction; the covariate that actually varies is the PHR span, which the arm-pair x span stratification reports alongside

tie_audit.note: 37% of the arm pairs are tied at similarity 0 in the published axis, so the published routine's ordinal ranking (ties broken by row order) is not the Spearman coefficient; both are reported and both give the same stage order

flaw_iii_satellite_reweighting.note: the arm-level statistic gives every arm pair the same weight, and arm pairs are not equally populated (satellite-rich blocks hold 3.80 PHR pairs on average, satellite-poor blocks 2.00), so the collapse moves the effective mean satellite fraction from 0.708 to 0.661 and the both-rich weight share from 0.636 to 0.552

contrast_ci_calibration_simulation.reading: at a nominal 95% level the paired dyadic interval covers the true zero in 0.930 of replicates (both regimes, so differencing is safe even when arm effects differ between stages), the arm-pair block bootstrap in 0.930, and the chromosome-end bootstrap in 0.990. All three are valid; the chromosome-end bootstrap is the conservative one, as expected with only 27 resampling units. A contrast that is resolvable at pair resolution and not at chromosome-end resolution is therefore a statement about how far the result generalises beyond the 27 ends sampled, not a contradiction

axis_change.verdict: there is no axis change to survive: analyses (1) and (2) use numerically the same similarity axis, so the axis cannot be the cause of the label change. The cause is the collapse of the 25.6% of pair-level variance that lives WITHIN arm pairs

satellite_control.verdict: the association and the zygotene-over-diplotene ordering survive both the satellite-rich subset and the partial correlation on the pair's mean satellite fraction; the satellite-POOR subset cannot test anything because it is q x q and its sequence axis is tied at zero

step_E_verdict.manuscript_sentence: Across four mouse meiotic stages the sequence-contact coupling is present at every stage (Spearman rho 0.42, 0.61, 0.58, 0.25 with dyadic standard errors clustered on both chromosome arms, all p <= 5.8e-09; arm-blocked permutation p <= 0.0015), is highest at zygotene and pachytene and lowest at diplotene (-0.33 relative to pachytene, dyadic 95% CI -0.37 to -0.29).
step_E_verdict.manuscript_sentence_not_allowed: 'the coupling is strongest at the zygotene bouquet' -- the zygotene and pachytene estimates differ by -0.038 with an arm bootstrap CI of -0.131 to +0.043, so the ordering between them is not resolvable; nor may the arm-level Mantel 'pachytene peak' be presented as a stage effect, because at the same axis the within-arm-pair variation -- which the arm-level statistic discards -- peaks at zygotene. The paired dyadic estimate of that difference is smaller still (-0.038, dyadic 95% CI -0.067 to -0.009, p=0.017) and it is not resolvable at all when the resampling unit is the chromosome end (95% CI -0.131 to +0.043); a 0.04 difference in rho between the two upper stages does not support an ordering

step_F_dyadic.which_design_to_report_and_why: report design 4 (dyadic two-way clustered inference at pair resolution) for the per-stage estimates, because designs 1 and 4 give identical point estimates while only 4 has a valid standard error, and it keeps all 1135 pairs instead of collapsing to 344 arm means. Report the stage contest with BOTH the dyadic CI and the chromosome-end bootstrap the referee asked for, because they disagree and the disagreement is itself the finding. Do not report design 2 (arm-level Mantel) as the primary analysis: it discards the within-arm-pair variation, gives every arm pair equal weight, and its peak label changes with the flank window

zygotene_minus_pachytene.reading: the zygotene-over-pachytene advantage (-0.0381 in rho) is resolvable when the resampling unit is the PHR pair (dyadic 95% CI -0.067 to -0.009) or the arm-pair block (-0.067 to -0.009), and is not resolvable when the unit is the chromosome end (-0.131 to +0.043). The dyadic interval is calibrated (0.930 coverage at a true difference of zero) and the chromosome-end interval is conservative (0.990), so the disagreement is about generalisation to unsampled chromosome ends, not about validity

unmeasurable_with_data_on_disk: a satellite-masked CONTACT axis (needs zuo2021_<stage>.mcool per-bin matrices; h5py/cooler absent, 0.3-0.5 Gpixel per stage) -- so 'satellite content does not drive the contact axis' is untested; only stratification and partial correlation are available
a satellite-masked SEQUENCE axis on the published odgi Jaccard (needs a pggb graph rebuild); the substitute PAF Jaccard is VOID
minor-satellite content of these windows (M6: the local Dfam library has no Mus minor-satellite family; the proxy recovers ~0)
non-satellite repeat content (TAR1, subterminal satellite, shared TE families): no RepeatMasker run on this box

any statement about which stage the ARM-LEVEL statistic favours beyond 1 Mb: the published arm matrix exists only for the 1 Mb flanks, so the 2 Mb and 4 Mb arm-level columns use an arm-mean of the 2 Mb / 4 Mb pair Jaccard, not the published matrix
statistical power for the satellite-poor (q x q) subset: 7 chromosome ends, 42 pairs, 8 distinct axis values

any stage-specific mechanistic claim: the contact values are reused verbatim from data/mouse_<stage>_phr_<res>bp_seqlevel.tsv, so a multi-mapping artefact inside the contact values is invisible here, and per-stage library depth is uncontrolled (the within-pair share normalisation that would control it is a different design and was not run)
